extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, attorneys, agents, and appellants preparing ex parte appeal briefs to the USPTO (Board of Patent Appeals/Interferences / PTAB)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on required contents, formatting, and arguments for an appeal brief filed under 37 CFR 41.37 in an ex parte patent appeal to the USPTO Board. Covers required items, procedural deadlines, evidentiary limits, and common pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness / Filing deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must file a brief under 37 CFR 41.37 within two months from the date of filing the notice of appeal under 37 CFR 41.31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal brief fee in an application or ex parte reexamination is $0.00; while the adjusted fee remains $0, the brief need not be accompanied by an attempt to pay the fee under 37 CFR 41.20(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 CFR 41.37 for briefs filed on/after Jan 23, 2012
rubrics_metrics.description: Any brief for which the notice of appeal was filed on or after January 23, 2012 must comply with the requirements set forth in current 37 CFR 41.37; a brief filed on or after that date that fails to comply with 37 CFR 41.37(c) shall be held to be non-compliant under 37 CFR 41.37(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mere filing of a document titled as a brief will not necessarily be considered to be in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single copy requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one copy of the appeal brief is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Technology Center and control number
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief, as well as every other document relating to an appeal, should indicate the number of the Technology Center (TC) to which the application or patent under reexamination is assigned and the application or reexamination control number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present arguments responsive to every ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant’s brief must present arguments responsive to every ground of rejection stated by the examiner in the Office action from which the appeal has been taken (as modified by any advisory action and/or pre-appeal brief conference decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a ground of rejection is not addressed in the brief, appellant has waived any challenge to that ground and the Board may summarily sustain it (unless the examiner subsequently withdrew the rejection). Merely considering a ground 'clearly improper' does not justify failing to explain why the examiner erred. Requesting that a rejection be held in abeyance does not meet the requirements and will be treated as a waiver (e.g., non‑statutory double patenting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Full statement of position with citations
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must set forth arguments and the basis therefor, with citations of the statutes, regulations, authorities and parts of the record relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential that the Board be provided with a brief fully stating the position of the appellant with respect to each ground so that no search of the Record is required. The brief should not incorporate or reference previous responses. A statement which merely points out what a claim recites will not be considered an argument for patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required items and headings in the order set forth by 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must have all of the required items under appropriate headings in the order indicated in 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headings are not required to be included if an item is not applicable (e.g., real party in interest is the inventor(s), or there are no related appeals); the Office may assume certain information if items are omitted as allowed by the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real party in interest statement (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying by name the real party in interest at the time the appeal brief is filed, except not required if the named inventor(s) are themselves the real party in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification allows Board members to comply with ethics regulations. Example wording is provided (e.g., 'The real party in interest is XXXX corporation, the assignee of record, which is a subsidiary of...' ). If the statement is omitted, the Office may assume the named inventor(s) are the real party in interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related appeals, interferences, and trials statement (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying by application, patent, appeal, interference, or trial number all other prior and pending appeals, interferences, trials before the Board, or judicial proceedings that involve an application or patent owned by the appellant or assignee and may be related to or affect the pending appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are no such related cases, the appellant is not required to include the statement; the rule does not require appellant to provide copies of decisions in related cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of claimed subject matter (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise explanation of the subject matter defined in each of the rejected independent claims, referring to the specification in the Record by page and line number or by paragraph number, and to drawings by reference characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each independent claim (and dependent claims argued separately) that contains a means-plus-function or step-plus-function under 35 U.S.C. 112(f), the concise explanation must identify the structure, material, or acts in the specification corresponding to each claimed function with specific references. Reference to the patent application publication does not satisfy this paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument content and scope (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: The arguments of appellant with respect to each ground of rejection and the basis therefor, including citations of statutes, regulations, authorities and parts of the Record relied on, should be presented and must explain why the examiner erred as to each contested ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any arguments or authorities not included in the appeal brief will be refused consideration by the Board for the present appeal except as provided in §§ 41.41, 41.47 and 41.52. Arguments first made at oral hearing are not normally entitled to consideration. A supplemental brief may be filed if new authority becomes available after filing the brief (e.g., a pertinent court decision published after the brief was filed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate headings/subheadings for each ground of rejection and for separately-argued claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Each ground of rejection must be argued under a separate heading which clearly identifies the ground being contested. For multiple claims under the same ground, claims may be argued separately, as a group, or as a subgroup, but must be placed under subheadings identifying the specific claim(s) by number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant groups claims, the Board may select a single claim from the group and decide on that basis. Failure to separately argue claims which appellant has grouped together constitutes a waiver of any argument that the Board must consider the patentability of any grouped claim separately. Appellant must use a subheading for each claim for which separate consideration is desired. Examples of possible heading/subheading formats are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims appendix requirements (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing a copy of the claims involved in the appeal is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy should be a clean copy and should not include markings such as brackets or underlining except for claims in a reissue application and certain reexamination proceedings. The copy should be double-spaced and the appendix should start on a new page. See MPEP §§ cited for reissue/reexamination specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on including new or non-admitted amendments/evidence (37 CFR 41.37(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 41.37(c)(2) prohibits inclusion in a brief of any new or non-admitted amendment, affidavit, or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant wishes to seek review of an examiner’s refusal to admit an amendment, affidavit or evidence, such review is by petition to the Director under 37 CFR 1.181. The time for filing that petition is based on the date the examiner refused to enter the amendment/evidence, not the date the brief is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro se appellant exception
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is prosecuted by the appellant pro se (no attorney or agent of record) and the brief was neither prepared nor signed by a registered practitioner, the brief of a pro se appellant which does not contain all items specified in 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1) will be accepted as long as it substantially complies with subparagraphs (i), (ii), (iv) and (v).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence appendix recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: While no longer required to include an evidence appendix, the Office strongly encourages receiving copies of the evidence relied upon (e.g., declarations, affidavits, evidence of secondary considerations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing copies ensures the Board considers the proper evidence and avoids confusion as to the particular evidence referenced. Alternatively, clearly identify the evidence relied upon with a description and the date of entry into the Image File Wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments/evidence entered only if entered by examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment or other evidence submitted under 37 CFR 1.116 or 37 CFR 41.33 will not be entered as part of the record for the appeal unless entered by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief must be directed to the claims and record as of time of appeal; withdrawing claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must be directed to the claims and to the record of the case as they appeared at the time of the appeal. If appellant wishes to remove claims from consideration on appeal, appellant must submit an amendment to cancel the claims from the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellant may choose not to present arguments or rely upon particular evidence as to certain claim rejections, but such arguments/evidence are waived for purposes of the appeal and the Board may summarily sustain any grounds of rejection not argued. Examiners should no longer cancel non-appealed claims under prior practice—37 CFR 41.31(c) supersedes Ex parte Ghuman.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional materials and minimum requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1) specifies minimum requirements for a brief; appellant may include additional items such as a list of references, table of contents, table of cases, copies of evidence entered by the examiner, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A brief is in compliance as long as it includes items (i) to (v) in the order set forth and does not include prohibited material (e.g., new evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Example format and content (suggested organization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example of a format and content for an appeal brief: (A) Identification page; (B) Table of Contents; (C) Real party in interest page(s); (D) Related appeals, interferences, and trials page(s); (E) Summary of claimed subject matter page(s); (F) Argument page(s); (G) Claims appendix page(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each item should start on a separate page. This example shows an acceptable organization but the regulatory minimum is items (i)-(v) in order.
